concept.name: Good-till-date order
concept.definition: An order that remains active until it is executed, canceled, or a trader-specified expiry date (or date-time) is reached, whichever comes first. It generalizes the day order and the GTC order by making the expiration explicit.
concept.intuition: It is a standing order with a calendar deadline: 'keep trying until Friday, then stop.'
concept.mechanics: The broker or venue carries the open balance across sessions; when the specified ExpireDate or ExpireTime is reached, any remaining quantity is expired (canceled) and reported back - in FIX with OrdStatus/ExecType = Expired. Each venue enforces its own maximum allowed lifetime.
concept.failure_modes: As with GTC orders, a resting GTD order can fill long after submission when market conditions have changed. Time-zone and session-boundary conventions for the expiry date differ across venues, so the order may die earlier or later than assumed.
concept.misconceptions: GTD does not expire at the start of the named date in all markets - some venues treat the order as valid through the end of that date's session, others at a specified time.
concept.example: Ahead of an earnings date you place a GTD limit buy at $40 expiring next Friday; it works all week, and any unfilled balance is canceled automatically when Friday's session ends.
